analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי opens the narrative frame. הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ בָּאָה describes the setting of the sun, and וְהִנֵּה introduces what appeared in the darkness.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces the Qal wayyiqtol יְהִי, third person masculine singular, used impersonally.

analysis.evidence: הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ בָּאָה describes the sun setting, and the following clause reports darkness.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a singular absolute noun of common gender. The noun takes feminine singular agreement with בָּאָה here.

analysis.evidence: The subject הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ is the sun, and the following clause וַעֲלָטָה הָיָה says it was dark. Together they place the scene after sunset.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third-person feminine singular, agreeing with הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ.

analysis.evidence: In וַעֲלָטָה הָיָה, עֲלָטָה names the deep darkness and הָיָה states that it was present after sunset. Together they mean “there was deep darkness.”
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: תַנּוּר עָשָׁן means literally “a furnace of smoke.” The parallel phrase וְלַפִּיד אֵשׁ, “and a torch of fire,” supports the reading “smoking firepot.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular, in the construct state before עָשָׁן. It has no prefix or suffix.
